component.name: Apricot Studio
component.summary: Trim a clip from a video without re-encoding decisions

description.p: Apricot Studio does one thing: it takes a video, lets you mark a start and an end, and writes out that section. It is built for pulling a highlight out of a screen-recorder replay buffer without opening a full editor.

There are no export settings to answer. Every parameter is read from the file you opened — container, codec, resolution, frame rate, colour, GOP structure and bitrate — so the clip behaves like the recording it came from. Audio is stream-copied rather than re-encoded, so it takes no loss at all.

When the start of your selection lands on a keyframe, nothing needs to be decoded and the clip is copied straight out of the source: near-instant, and byte-for-byte identical. The app tells you which of the two paths an export will take before you run it.

ul.li: Instant, lossless export when the cut starts on a keyframe
Timeline with a filmstrip, audio waveform and keyframe markers
Quality presets that scale against the source, or a target file size
Per-track audio selection for recordings with separate mic and desktop
Optionally move the original to the wastebasket after exporting

description.p: A video kept outside Videos, Pictures or Downloads used to be reported as missing, because a sandboxed app cannot see it at all. Apricot Studio now recognises that and says so.

ul.li: Locate the file to open it once, or copy the command that allows its folder for good
Opening such a file from the file manager starts the app and explains, rather than appearing to fail
Clips are written to Videos when the source folder cannot take them
